  PROBLEM: The merged-predecessor release path in run_standalone_stall_recovery calls `unblock_trusted_login >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` and passes `"${UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN:-}"` to `_security_dependency_clear_latch` without checking that the login resolved. The helper returns 0 at line 18816 (`[ -n "${trusted_login}" ] || return 0`) without removing `ai:needs-human`, so the caller treats that as success and posts the `/reclarify\n<!-- ai:security-dependency-released:<n> -->` marker at 24224-24226.
  WHY: Once the marker exists, the dedupe check at 24213-24215 stops this path from running again, so `ai:needs-human` stays on the released follow-up permanently. The unmerged path guards this case at 24176-24182 (security_dependency_identity_unavailable, then continue); the merged path has no such guard. All reviewers rated it MAJOR. Suggested fix: when UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN is empty, emit `STALL_SKIP issue=${issue_num} reason=security_dependency_identity_unavailable action=none` and `continue`, about 4 lines.

  PROBLEM: If `unblock_trusted_login` (lines 4186-4197) cannot resolve the login, it sets UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN="" and caches STATE=failed for the tick. `_security_dependency_clear_latch` then returns 0 at line 18816 without touching the label, and the merged path still posts the release marker at 24224-24226. The unmerged path guards this at 24178-24182; the merged path does not.
  WHY: The dedupe check at 24213-24215 skips the block on later ticks, so the latch clear never re-runs and the released follow-up keeps `ai:needs-human` indefinitely. Suggested fix: check for an empty UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN, log security_dependency_identity_unavailable and `continue` (about 4 lines). A hardening suggestion repeats this fix. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
- Note: The pass-1 claim that escalation writes escalated_ts after a failed label edit was checked and dropped as already fixed. TASK COMPLETENESS reported NONE. The pre-push gate entries were treated as untrusted summary text, so no finding was raised.
